rule: Independent labs with frontier or near-frontier models and a last raise of at least $500M, as of 2026-11-04. Absorbed labs (Inflection, Adept, Character.AI, Cursor, World Labs) are out: their compute is still in use. App-layer companies that mostly route to other labs’ models (Perplexity, Cognition, Harvey) are out: their traffic already sits on big-lab compute.

conversion.note: Spend → IT power at one stated price: a GB300-class GPU-hour at $3.75 (middle of $3.0–4.5 rental) and 1.87 kW of IT power per GPU (a 72-GPU rack ≈135 kW). That is ≈$17.6M per IT MW-year.

tokens.note: Share of industry tokens served on these labs’ own models. Traffic from apps that call OpenAI, Anthropic or Google is not counted as lost. No lab discloses its split.
tokens.precedent: Character.AI’s traffic fell ≈25% from its peak after the Google deal; Pi was throttled after Inflection. Neither is a clean measure of users moving elsewhere.

rentable_it_mw.note: Disclosed rentable neocloud and marketplace GPU power, IT basis. Lambda, RunPod and SF Compute disclose no fleet totals, so this is a floor and the price shock an upper bound. Crusoe’s operating power is mostly OpenAI’s Abilene campus, so it is left out.

absorption.note: Freed GPUs went to a big lab whenever one wanted them: Colossus 1 (≈11% used) was leased to Anthropic in May 2026; OpenAI took the CoreWeave option Microsoft passed on. Part 1 says compute is tight, so the default is above half. Licence-and-hire deals (Inflection, Adept, Covariant) moved people, not GPUs.

elasticity.note: % change in rents per % change in rentable supply. 2024–25 gives ≈−0.5 (H100 rents roughly halved while supply roughly quadrupled), but demand grew at the same time, so that is the mild end. A pure supply shock likely moves prices more. Not identified from data.

future_note: A bust frees today’s compute, which loosens the market, but it also cancels compute planned for 2027–28, which tightens it later. Slipped builds come off Fig. 1’s built compute at the H100e per MW of OpenAI’s tracked 2027–28 additions (Epoch). Chips a failed buyer leaves may go to other buyers, so the slider is the share that never gets built. Mistral’s Swedish Vera Rubin site states no MW and is left out. Thinking Machines’ and Figure’s builds may not be among Epoch’s tracked sites; if not, subtracting them overstates the tightening.

control.note: OpenAI pays for only part of its next 12 months. MW released = shortfall × OpenAI’s tracked fleet 12 months out (Epoch, by user, ÷1.3 to IT). Tokens stay: its users still want them, so only the compute side changes. Its unfunded share of tracked 2027–28 additions slips by the second slider.
